# abuse

```go
import "github.com/its-ernest/http-keystone/abuse"
```

Package abuse provides behavioral analysis middleware for Echo v5. It tracks client reputation via a scoring system to mitigate scrapers and scanners.

## Variables

<a name="DefaultConfig"></a>DefaultConfig provides the standard settings for abuse detection middleware.

```go
var DefaultConfig = Config{
    Skipper:   middleware.DefaultSkipper,
    KeyFunc:   func(c *echo.Context) string { return c.RealIP() },
    Threshold: 100,
    Cooldown:  30 * time.Minute,
    MaxDelay:  2 * time.Second,
    DelayFunc: func(score int) time.Duration {
        return time.Duration(score) * 10 * time.Millisecond
    },
    ErrorHandler: func(c *echo.Context, score int) error {
        return echo.NewHTTPError(http.StatusForbidden, "Access denied due to suspicious activity")
    },
}
```

<a name="New"></a>
## func [New](<https://github.com/its-ernest/http-keystone/blob/main/abuse/middleware.go#L95>)

```go
func New(config Config) echo.MiddlewareFunc
```

New returns an Echo middleware that monitors and limits abusive behavior. It should be placed early in the middleware stack to protect downstream resources.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"github.com/its-ernest/http-keystone/abuse"
	"github.com/labstack/echo/v5"
)

func main() {
	e := echo.New()

	// Instant-ban on sensitive files, warn on API spam
	e.Use(abuse.New(abuse.Config{
		Threshold: 100,
		Rules: []abuse.Rule{
			// immediate ban for ANY attempt on .env
			{Path: "/.env", Score: 100},

			// heavy score only for POST requests to login (brute force protection)
			{Path: "/api/v1/login", Method: "POST", Score: 20},

			// light score for general API exploration
			{Path: "/api/v1/*", Method: "GET", Score: 2},
		},
	}))
}
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="NewForwardedIPKeyFunc"></a>
## func [NewForwardedIPKeyFunc](<https://github.com/its-ernest/http-keystone/blob/main/abuse/middleware.go#L243>)

```go
func NewForwardedIPKeyFunc(options ...echo.TrustOption) func(c *echo.Context) string
```

NewForwardedIPKeyFunc returns a KeyFunc that resolves the client IP from X\-Forwarded\-For, trusting only the direct peer when that peer is a trusted proxy. Pass echo.TrustIPRange \(and the other echo.Trust\* options\) to describe your proxies; by default loopback, link\-local and private ranges are trusted.

Use it when the middleware runs behind a reverse proxy and you do not want to set echo.Echo.IPExtractor globally:

```
e.Use(abuse.New(abuse.Config{
	Store:   counter,
	KeyFunc: abuse.NewForwardedIPKeyFunc(echo.TrustIPRange(proxyCIDR)),
}))
```

Without trusted proxies \(for example when the app faces the internet directly\), use echo.ExtractIPDirect with NewIPKeyFunc so headers are ignored completely.

<a name="Config"></a>
## type [Config](<https://github.com/its-ernest/http-keystone/blob/main/abuse/middleware.go#L35-L75>)

Config defines the settings for the abuse detection middleware.

```go
type Config struct {
    // Skipper defines a function to skip middleware. Defaults to
    // middleware.DefaultSkipper.
    Skipper middleware.Skipper

    // KeyFunc derives the identity used to track heat. The returned string
    // is appended to "abuse:heat:" as the store key.
    //
    // The default is c.RealIP(). Note that c.RealIP() trusts
    // X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP when Echo has an IPExtractor configured,
    // and Echo's default extracts the header values without verification.
    // Behind a proxy, configure e.IPExtractor (see
    // echo.ExtractIPFromXFFHeader) or set KeyFunc to something the client
    // cannot choose. See NewForwardedIPKeyFunc for a ready-made helper.
    KeyFunc func(c *echo.Context) string

    Store store.Counter
    // Threshold is the heat score at which requests are rejected.
    // Values <= 0 fall back to DefaultConfig.Threshold (100) so a zero
    // Config can never block every request.
    Threshold int
    Rules     []Rule
    // Cooldown is how long heat is remembered. Values <= 0 fall back to
    // DefaultConfig.Cooldown (30 minutes).
    Cooldown time.Duration
    // EnableDelay adds latency to suspicious requests instead of a hard block.
    EnableDelay bool
    // MaxDelay caps the tarpit delay applied when EnableDelay is set.
    // Values <= 0 fall back to DefaultConfig.MaxDelay (2s).
    MaxDelay time.Duration
    // DelayFunc computes the tarpit delay for a heat score. The result is
    // clamped to MaxDelay and never exceeds it.
    // Values <= 0 mean no delay.
    // Default is a linear curve of score*10ms (e.g. 75 heat -> 750ms).
    DelayFunc func(score int) time.Duration
    // Jitter adds +/-20% randomness to the computed delay so delayed
    // clients do not retry in lockstep. The clamped MaxDelay is still
    // honoured.
    Jitter       bool
    ErrorHandler func(c *echo.Context, score int) error
}
```

<a name="Rule"></a>
## type [Rule](<https://github.com/its-ernest/http-keystone/blob/main/abuse/middleware.go#L21-L32>)

Rule defines the "heat" points added for specific path patterns. Path supports exact matches \(e.g., "/.env"\) and a trailing "\*" wildcard on a path\-segment boundary: "/admin\*" matches "/admin" and "/admin/config" but not "/administrator".

```go
type Rule struct {
    // Path is the URL path to match. It supports exact matches and a
    // trailing "*" wildcard on a path-segment boundary; Echo's router is
    // not involved. Matching is case-sensitive and ignores query strings.
    Path string

    // Method is the HTTP method to match (GET, POST, etc.). Empty means match all.
    Method string

    // Score is the amount of *heat* to add when this rule matches
    Score int
}
```
